texts.title: Picatrix
texts.description: The Latin Picatrix is the principal medieval Latin witness to the Arabic Ghayat al-hakim and a central source for astral image magic.

texts.title: Ars Notoria
texts.description: The Ars Notoria is a ritual art of memory and learning transmitted in medieval Latin manuscripts.

texts.title: Sworn Book of Honorius
texts.description: The Sworn Book of Honorius is a major medieval ritual magic text concerned with divine vision, angelic hierarchy, and ritual discipline.

texts.title: Forbidden Rites
texts.description: Richard Kieckhefer's Forbidden Rites edits and studies a fifteenth-century necromantic manual.

texts.title: The Transformations of Magic
texts.description: Frank Klaassen's study examines illicit learned magic in the later Middle Ages and Renaissance.

texts.title: Magic in the Cloister
texts.description: Sophie Page's monograph examines monastic and clerical engagements with occult approaches to the medieval universe.

texts.title: Invoking Angels
texts.description: Claire Fanger's edited collection studies theurgic ideas and practices from the thirteenth to sixteenth centuries.

texts.title: Unlocked Books
texts.description: Benedek Lang's study of manuscripts of learned magic in Central European libraries foregrounds codicology, ownership, and library context as evidence for learned magical transmission.

texts.title: Magic in Medieval Manuscripts
texts.description: Sophie Page's study examines medieval manuscript evidence for magical texts and the codicological contexts in which occult, devotional, and scientific materials circulated.

texts.title: Hazards of the Dark Arts
texts.description: Richard Kieckhefer's translation and study of Johannes Hartlieb's advice for princes places witchcraft, magic, and prohibited arts within fifteenth-century political and moral counsel.

texts.title: Liber Theysolius
texts.description: The Liber Theysolius is a medieval text associated in recent scholarship with wisdom, familiar spirits, and the pursuit of knowledge through ritualized contact.

texts.title: Liber Juratus Honorii
texts.description: The Liber Juratus Honorii, or Sworn Book of Honorius, is a major Latin ritual text concerning divine vision, angelic hierarchy, and sworn secrecy.

texts.title: Liber Razielis
texts.description: The Liber Razielis is a Latin textual complex associated with angelic revelation, astral knowledge, and the figure of Raziel.

texts.title: De radiis
texts.description: De radiis, associated with al-Kindi in Latin tradition, theorizes rays, celestial causality, and the efficacy of words and images in medieval natural philosophy.

texts.title: De imaginibus
texts.description: De imaginibus is a Latin astral-image text attributed to Thabit ibn Qurra and important for theories of talismanic images and celestial timing.

texts.title: Speculum astronomiae
texts.description: The Speculum astronomiae classifies astrological and image-making texts and became a crucial witness for scholastic attempts to distinguish licit astronomy from illicit image magic.

texts.title: A History of Magic and Experimental Science
texts.description: Lynn Thorndike's multi-volume history framed magic and experimental science as intertwined parts of medieval intellectual history, even where later scholarship has revised its assumptions.

texts.title: Clavicula Salomonis
texts.description: The Key of Solomon is a major Solomonic grimoire tradition transmitted in late medieval and early modern manuscripts, important for ritual purity, seals, conjurations, and textual instability.

texts.title: Hygromanteia
texts.description: The Hygromanteia is a Byzantine Greek Solomonic ritual tradition that stands behind later Key of Solomon materials and complicates Latin-centered grimoire histories.

texts.title: Testament of Solomon
texts.description: The Testament of Solomon is a late antique demonological text that made Solomon a paradigmatic commander of spirits in later magical and literary traditions.

texts.title: Liber de angelis
texts.description: The Liber de angelis names a family of Latin ritual texts concerned with angelic knowledge, invocation, and the textual authority of revealed ritual.

texts.title: Liber visionum
texts.description: The Liber visionum is associated with John of Morigny's visionary and ritual reworking of Ars Notoria materials.

texts.title: Flowers of Heavenly Teaching
texts.description: The Flowers of Heavenly Teaching names John of Morigny's revised ritual and visionary project for divinely assisted knowledge.

texts.title: Munich Manual
texts.description: The Munich Manual is the fifteenth-century necromantic manuscript edited and analyzed by Richard Kieckhefer in Forbidden Rites.

texts.title: Book of Oberon
texts.description: The Book of Oberon is an early modern English ritual magic compilation that preserves and transforms medieval Solomonic and spirit-conjuring materials.

texts.title: Book of Soyga
texts.description: The Book of Soyga is an early modern angelological and cryptographic ritual text associated with John Dee and earlier learned magical traditions.

texts.title: Heptameron
texts.description: The Heptameron is a ritual magic text attributed to Pietro d'Abano in print tradition and central to early modern angelic and planetary conjuration.

texts.title: Ars Almadel
texts.description: The Ars Almadel is a Solomonic angelic ritual text transmitted in early modern grimoire compilations and linked to older angelic invocation traditions.

texts.title: Ars Paulina
texts.description: The Ars Paulina is a Solomonic text of planetary and zodiacal angelic invocation preserved in early modern Lemegeton traditions.

texts.title: Ars Goetia
texts.description: The Ars Goetia is an early modern Solomonic demon catalogue and conjuring text whose roots and reception belong to the wider grimoire tradition.

texts.title: Lemegeton
texts.description: The Lemegeton or Lesser Key of Solomon is an early modern Solomonic compilation whose parts preserve angelic, demonic, and planetary ritual traditions.

texts.title: Grimorium Verum
texts.description: Grimorium Verum is an early modern printed grimoire important for the post-medieval reception and reorganization of spirit conjuration traditions.

texts.title: Sixth and Seventh Books of Moses
texts.description: The Sixth and Seventh Books of Moses are early modern/modern grimoire traditions relevant to the long reception of biblical magical authority.

texts.title: Liber Lunae
texts.description: The Liber Lunae is a Latin lunar and astral ritual text associated with image magic, timing, and the broader learned magical manuscript corpus.

texts.title: De occultis operibus naturae
texts.description: De occultis operibus naturae names a scholastic problem field concerning hidden natural powers, occult properties, and the boundary between nature and magic.

texts.title: Secretum Secretorum
texts.description: The Secretum Secretorum is a pseudo-Aristotelian mirror-for-princes and knowledge compendium whose medieval reception intersects with astrology, physiognomy, medicine, and occult counsel.

texts.title: Opus Majus
texts.description: Roger Bacon's Opus Majus is central to medieval discussions of experiment, language, optics, astrology, and the status of knowledge later associated with magic and science.

texts.title: De universo
texts.description: William of Auvergne's De universo is central to theological discussion of spirits, demons, image magic, and the created order.

texts.title: Etymologiae
texts.description: Isidore of Seville's Etymologiae transmitted influential classifications of magic, divination, and pagan learning to medieval encyclopedic culture.

texts.title: De mineralibus
texts.description: Albertus Magnus's De mineralibus is important for scholastic discussion of stones, occult properties, natural powers, and lapidary traditions.

texts.title: De divinatione daemonum
texts.description: Augustine's De divinatione daemonum helped shape Christian explanations of divination, demons, signs, and illicit curiosity.

texts.title: Liber experimentorum
texts.description: Liber experimentorum names a family or genre of experiment-books in medieval learned magic, where recipes, trials, secrets, and operations circulate as textual experiments rather than stable authored treatises.

texts.title: Buch aller verbotenen Kunst
texts.description: Johannes Hartlieb's Buch aller verbotenen Kunst, or Book of All Forbidden Arts, is a fifteenth-century German treatment of prohibited arts, witchcraft, and magical practices for princely and moral instruction.

persons.name: Richard Kieckhefer
persons.description: Learned magic, necromancy, and the social history of medieval ritual texts.

persons.name: Claire Fanger
persons.description: Medieval ritual magic, angelic theurgy, and visionary autobiographical writing.

persons.name: Frank Klaassen
persons.description: Manuscript culture and transformations of learned magic in late medieval and early modern England.

persons.name: Sophie Page
persons.description: Monastic, clerical, and manuscript contexts for medieval occult learning.

persons.name: Michael D. Bailey
persons.description: Medieval religion, superstition, witchcraft, and magic as contested categories.

persons.name: Catherine Rider
persons.description: Medieval magic, medicine, fertility, charms, and pastoral contexts.

persons.name: Dan Attrell
persons.description: Translator and scholar of the Latin Picatrix and astral magic.

persons.name: David Porreca
persons.description: Medieval Latin Hermetica, Picatrix studies, and transmission of Arabic astral magic.

persons.name: Apollonius of Tyana
persons.description: Ancient sage whose name became attached to medieval ritual and talismanic traditions.

persons.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
persons.description: Ninth-century Sabian scholar associated in Latin reception with astral image theory.

persons.name: Benedek Lang
persons.description: Central European manuscript libraries, learned magic, and the codicological history of ritual texts.

persons.name: Lynn Thorndike
persons.description: Early twentieth-century historian whose multi-volume history made magic and experimental science a continuous object of medieval intellectual history.

persons.name: Nicolas Weill-Parot
persons.description: Historian of astral image theory, scholastic natural philosophy, and the boundary between licit and illicit image practices.

persons.name: Jean-Patrice Boudet
persons.description: Historian of medieval astrology, divination, learned magic, and manuscript transmission in the Latin West.

persons.name: Julien Veronese
persons.description: Scholar of ritual magic, the Ars Notoria, and manuscript traditions of angelic and learned ritual practice.

persons.name: Johannes Hartlieb
persons.description: Fifteenth-century Bavarian physician and author of advice literature on forbidden arts, witchcraft, and princely governance.

persons.name: Ulrich Molitor
persons.description: Late medieval jurist and author associated with learned discussion of witchcraft and demonic magic.

persons.name: John of Morigny
persons.description: Fourteenth-century Benedictine monk whose visionary autobiography and ritual book reworked the Ars Notoria in Marian and monastic terms.

persons.name: Honorius of Thebes
persons.description: Attributed authorial figure attached to the Sworn Book of Honorius and traditions of angelic ritual magic.

persons.name: Raziel
persons.description: Angelic authority associated with the Liber Razielis and related Jewish and Latin traditions of revealed esoteric knowledge.

persons.name: Solomon
persons.description: Biblical king whose attributed authority structures major medieval and early modern traditions of spirit command, talismanic lore, and ritual experiment.

persons.name: Theysolius
persons.description: Attributed or textual authority associated with the Liber Theysolius and traditions concerning familiar spirits and wisdom.

persons.name: David Pingree
persons.description: Historian of exact sciences, astrology, and astral magic whose work is essential for Arabic, Greek, Sanskrit, and Latin transmission histories.

persons.name: Valerie Flint
persons.description: Historian of early medieval religion and magic whose work shaped debates about Christianization, pastoral care, and magical survivals.

persons.name: Robert Mathiesen
persons.description: Scholar of ritual magic manuscripts and Solomonic textual traditions, especially relevant to Ars Notoria and grimoire transmission.

persons.name: Jan R. Veenstra
persons.description: Historian of magic, learned culture, and intellectual history whose work connects medieval classifications to Renaissance magic.

persons.name: Charles Burnett
persons.description: Historian of Arabic-Latin transmission, astrology, natural philosophy, and occult sciences in the medieval Latin West.

persons.name: Paola Zambelli
persons.description: Historian of astrology, magic, scholastic debates, and the Speculum astronomiae tradition.

persons.name: Agostino Paravicini Bagliani
persons.description: Historian of medieval learned culture, astrology, medicine, and courtly/scientific contexts relevant to occult knowledge.

persons.name: Don C. Skemer
persons.description: Manuscript scholar whose work on textual amulets and written protection is central for charms and apotropaic writing.

persons.name: Lea T. Olsan
persons.description: Scholar of charms, healing prayers, and vernacular ritual language in medieval manuscript contexts.

persons.name: Katelyn Mesler
persons.description: Scholar of Jewish, Christian, and ritual magic traditions, including Solomonic and angelological transmission.

persons.name: Florence Chave-Mahir
persons.description: Scholar of exorcism, liturgy, ritual authority, and the borderlands of religious and magical practice.

persons.name: Béatrice Delaurenti
persons.description: Historian of medieval knowledge, marvels, nature, and the conceptual edges of natural and occult causality.

persons.name: Roger Bacon
persons.description: Thirteenth-century Franciscan philosopher whose discussions of experiment, language, optics, astrology, and natural powers are central to medieval debates over knowledge and magic.

persons.name: Albertus Magnus
persons.description: Thirteenth-century Dominican philosopher whose authority shaped scholastic natural philosophy, astrology, minerals, animals, and debates over occult properties.

persons.name: Thomas Aquinas
persons.description: Thirteenth-century Dominican theologian whose discussions of demons, superstition, divination, and illicit pact shaped later scholastic classifications of magic.

persons.name: William of Auvergne
persons.description: Thirteenth-century bishop and theologian whose treatment of demons, image magic, and illicit ritual is central to medieval demonological classification.

persons.name: Pietro d'Abano
persons.description: Italian physician and philosopher associated with astrology, astral causality, and later magical attributions.

persons.name: Arnald of Villanova
persons.description: Physician and religious writer whose attributed corpus became entangled with medical, alchemical, and astrological materials.

persons.name: John of Salisbury
persons.description: Twelfth-century cleric whose critique of courtly divination and occult practices is important for earlier medieval moral classification.

persons.name: Nicole Oresme
persons.description: Fourteenth-century philosopher and bishop whose criticism of astrology and divination belongs to late medieval debates over celestial influence.

persons.name: Augustine of Hippo
persons.description: Late antique Christian theologian whose account of demons, signs, superstition, and illicit curiosity shaped medieval classifications of magic.

persons.name: Isidore of Seville
persons.description: Early medieval encyclopedist whose etymological classifications of magic, divination, and pagan learning shaped later reference traditions.

persons.name: al-Kindi
persons.description: Arabic philosopher associated in Latin reception with De radiis and theories of rays, causality, words, and celestial influence.

persons.name: Abu Ma'shar
persons.description: Ninth-century astrologer whose works shaped Latin astrology and the learned background for astral magic and image theory.

persons.name: Adelard of Bath
persons.description: Twelfth-century translator and natural philosopher whose Arabic-Latin learning helped shape Latin debates about astrology, natural causality, and experiment.

persons.name: Hugh of Saint-Victor
persons.description: Twelfth-century theologian whose classifications of arts, knowledge, and illicit curiosity form part of the scholastic background for later treatments of magic.

persons.name: Bernard Silvester
persons.description: Twelfth-century intellectual associated with cosmological and astrological learning in the Latin schools, important for the learned background of celestial influence.

persons.name: Peter Abelard
persons.description: Twelfth-century theologian whose discussions of divination and astrology belong to earlier scholastic attempts to delimit illicit knowledge.

persons.name: Cecco d'Ascoli
persons.description: Fourteenth-century astrologer and poet whose condemnation and execution made him a key figure in debates over astrology, determinism, and forbidden knowledge.

persons.name: Michael Scot
persons.description: Thirteenth-century translator, astrologer, and court intellectual associated with Arabic-Latin science and later magical reputation.

concepts.label: Medieval Magic
concepts.definition_short: Medieval magic is an Analyst Term for practices, accusations, texts, and learned theories that modern scholars group under magic while medieval actors used more specific categories such as nigromantia, superstitio, experimentum, and scientia imaginum.
concepts.significance: Medieval magic is an Analyst Term for practices, accusations, texts, and learned theories that modern scholars group under magic while medieval actors used more specific categories such as nigromantia, superstitio, experimentum, and scientia imaginum.

concepts.label: Ars Notoria
concepts.definition_short: Ars Notoria is an Actor Term for a medieval ritual art of learning that joined prayers, notae, angelic invocation, and claims of accelerated intellectual acquisition.
concepts.significance: Ars Notoria is an Actor Term for a medieval ritual art of learning that joined prayers, notae, angelic invocation, and claims of accelerated intellectual acquisition.

concepts.label: Nigromantia
concepts.definition_short: Nigromantia is a medieval Latin Actor Term often used for illicit ritual operations involving spirits, frequently blurred by clerical writers with necromancy and demonic magic.
concepts.significance: Nigromantia is a medieval Latin Actor Term often used for illicit ritual operations involving spirits, frequently blurred by clerical writers with necromancy and demonic magic.

concepts.label: Astral Image Magic
concepts.definition_short: Astral image magic is an Analyst Term for learned practices that connect images, planetary timing, materials, and celestial influence in Arabic and Latin scholastic settings.
concepts.significance: Astral image magic is an Analyst Term for learned practices that connect images, planetary timing, materials, and celestial influence in Arabic and Latin scholastic settings.

concepts.label: Picatrix Tradition
concepts.definition_short: The Picatrix tradition denotes the Arabic-to-Latin transmission of the Ghayat al-hakim and its reception as a major source for medieval and Renaissance astral magic.
concepts.significance: The Picatrix tradition denotes the Arabic-to-Latin transmission of the Ghayat al-hakim and its reception as a major source for medieval and Renaissance astral magic.

concepts.label: Grimoire
concepts.definition_short: Grimoire is primarily an Analyst Term for manuscript or printed collections of ritual instructions, spirit lists, conjurations, prayers, and experiments.
concepts.significance: Grimoire is primarily an Analyst Term for manuscript or printed collections of ritual instructions, spirit lists, conjurations, prayers, and experiments.

concepts.label: Superstitio
concepts.definition_short: Superstitio is a Latin Actor Term used by theologians and pastoral writers to classify improper religious practice, divination, charms, and illicit ritual dependence.
concepts.significance: Superstitio is a Latin Actor Term used by theologians and pastoral writers to classify improper religious practice, divination, charms, and illicit ritual dependence.

concepts.label: Learned Magic
concepts.definition_short: Learned magic is an Analyst Term for textually transmitted practices cultivated by literate clerical, university, monastic, or courtly actors.
concepts.significance: Learned magic is an Analyst Term for textually transmitted practices cultivated by literate clerical, university, monastic, or courtly actors.

concepts.label: Familiar Spirit
concepts.definition_short: Familiar spirit is an Actor Term in many late medieval and early modern contexts for a spirit bound to, assisting, or repeatedly contacted by a practitioner; modern scholars use the category cautiously because legal, literary, and ritual sources describe such spirits in different registers.
concepts.significance: Familiar spirit is an Actor Term in many late medieval and early modern contexts for a spirit bound to, assisting, or repeatedly contacted by a practitioner; modern scholars use the category cautiously because legal, literary, and ritual sources describe such spirits in different registers.

concepts.label: Magic and Cognition
concepts.definition_short: Magic and cognition is an Analyst Term for scholarship that studies medieval magical practice through memory, perception, learning, ritual attention, and the mental operations implied by diagrams, prayers, images, and repeated procedures.
concepts.significance: Magic and cognition is an Analyst Term for scholarship that studies medieval magical practice through memory, perception, learning, ritual attention, and the mental operations implied by diagrams, prayers, images, and repeated procedures.

concepts.label: Manuscript Miscellany
concepts.definition_short: Manuscript miscellany is an Analyst Term for codices that collect heterogeneous texts; in medieval magic scholarship it matters because ritual, medical, devotional, astrological, and divinatory materials often survive together rather than in isolated genre books.
concepts.significance: Manuscript miscellany is an Analyst Term for codices that collect heterogeneous texts; in medieval magic scholarship it matters because ritual, medical, devotional, astrological, and divinatory materials often survive together rather than in isolated genre books.

concepts.label: Clerical Underworld
concepts.definition_short: Clerical underworld is an Analyst Term associated especially with Richard Kieckhefer's account of literate clerics who copied, adapted, and used illicit ritual texts while remaining within ecclesiastical culture.
concepts.significance: Clerical underworld is an Analyst Term associated especially with Richard Kieckhefer's account of literate clerics who copied, adapted, and used illicit ritual texts while remaining within ecclesiastical culture.

concepts.label: Angelic Invocation
concepts.definition_short: Angelic invocation names ritual address to angels in medieval texts; it may function as an actor practice in prayer-based ritual books and as an analyst category for the study of theurgic or devotional magic.
concepts.significance: Angelic invocation names ritual address to angels in medieval texts; it may function as an actor practice in prayer-based ritual books and as an analyst category for the study of theurgic or devotional magic.

concepts.label: Demonic Pact
concepts.definition_short: Demonic pact is a theological and legal category used to explain illicit magic as explicit or implicit agreement with demons, while modern historians analyze it as a polemical and juridical tool rather than a transparent description of practice.
concepts.significance: Demonic pact is a theological and legal category used to explain illicit magic as explicit or implicit agreement with demons, while modern historians analyze it as a polemical and juridical tool rather than a transparent description of practice.

concepts.label: Necromancy
concepts.definition_short: Necromancy is an Analyst Term in much modern scholarship for learned spirit-conjuring practices, although medieval Latin nigromantia often carried broader associations with illicit demonic magic rather than the literal raising of the dead.
concepts.significance: Necromancy is an Analyst Term in much modern scholarship for learned spirit-conjuring practices, although medieval Latin nigromantia often carried broader associations with illicit demonic magic rather than the literal raising of the dead.

concepts.label: Divination
concepts.definition_short: Divination covers practices for obtaining hidden knowledge, from geomancy and sortilege to astrological judgment; medieval sources classify it variously as natural, superstitious, demonic, or licit depending on method and authority.
concepts.significance: Divination covers practices for obtaining hidden knowledge, from geomancy and sortilege to astrological judgment; medieval sources classify it variously as natural, superstitious, demonic, or licit depending on method and authority.

concepts.label: Geomancy
concepts.definition_short: Geomancy is an Actor Term for a learned divinatory art based on figures generated by points or marks and interpreted through structured houses, often circulating with astrology and other clerical arts.
concepts.significance: Geomancy is an Actor Term for a learned divinatory art based on figures generated by points or marks and interpreted through structured houses, often circulating with astrology and other clerical arts.

concepts.label: Chiromancy
concepts.definition_short: Chiromancy is an Actor Term for palmistry or hand-reading, a divinatory practice treated in medieval manuals and often debated within broader classifications of natural signs and illicit prediction.
concepts.significance: Chiromancy is an Actor Term for palmistry or hand-reading, a divinatory practice treated in medieval manuals and often debated within broader classifications of natural signs and illicit prediction.

concepts.label: Charms
concepts.definition_short: Charms is an Analyst Term for spoken, written, or performed formulae used for healing, protection, coercion, or divination; the category requires care because medieval sources may frame the same materials as prayer, medicine, superstition, or magic.
concepts.significance: Charms is an Analyst Term for spoken, written, or performed formulae used for healing, protection, coercion, or divination; the category requires care because medieval sources may frame the same materials as prayer, medicine, superstition, or magic.

concepts.label: Amulets
concepts.definition_short: Amulets are objects worn or carried for protection, healing, or influence, frequently combining inscriptions, images, materials, and ritual timing in ways that cross medical, devotional, and magical classifications.
concepts.significance: Amulets are objects worn or carried for protection, healing, or influence, frequently combining inscriptions, images, materials, and ritual timing in ways that cross medical, devotional, and magical classifications.

concepts.label: Talismans
concepts.definition_short: Talismans are crafted objects intended to mediate celestial, spiritual, or symbolic power; in medieval scholarship the term often overlaps with image magic, astral magic, and Arabic-Latin theories of celestial influence.
concepts.significance: Talismans are crafted objects intended to mediate celestial, spiritual, or symbolic power; in medieval scholarship the term often overlaps with image magic, astral magic, and Arabic-Latin theories of celestial influence.

concepts.label: Suffumigation
concepts.definition_short: Suffumigation is an Actor Term for ritual fumigation with incense, herbs, or other substances, often coordinated with planetary timing, spirit address, purification, or image consecration.
concepts.significance: Suffumigation is an Actor Term for ritual fumigation with incense, herbs, or other substances, often coordinated with planetary timing, spirit address, purification, or image consecration.

concepts.label: Characters and Seals
concepts.definition_short: Characters and seals are graphic signs used in ritual, talismanic, and angelic materials; they matter as manuscript phenomena because their transmission depends on visual copying as much as verbal text.
concepts.significance: Characters and seals are graphic signs used in ritual, talismanic, and angelic materials; they matter as manuscript phenomena because their transmission depends on visual copying as much as verbal text.

concepts.label: Voces Magicae
concepts.definition_short: Voces magicae is an Analyst Term for nonordinary ritual words, names, and syllables whose efficacy is attached to sound, secrecy, antiquity, or divine and angelic names.
concepts.significance: Voces magicae is an Analyst Term for nonordinary ritual words, names, and syllables whose efficacy is attached to sound, secrecy, antiquity, or divine and angelic names.

concepts.label: Ritual Purity
concepts.definition_short: Ritual purity names requirements of confession, fasting, abstinence, cleanliness, prayer, or moral preparation that structure many medieval ritual magic texts and blur devotional and magical categories.
concepts.significance: Ritual purity names requirements of confession, fasting, abstinence, cleanliness, prayer, or moral preparation that structure many medieval ritual magic texts and blur devotional and magical categories.

concepts.label: Condemned Arts
concepts.definition_short: Condemned arts is a hybrid category for practices classified as illicit by theologians, jurists, pastoral writers, or university authorities, including divination, demonic invocation, image magic, and suspect ritual learning.
concepts.significance: Condemned arts is a hybrid category for practices classified as illicit by theologians, jurists, pastoral writers, or university authorities, including divination, demonic invocation, image magic, and suspect ritual learning.

concepts.label: Grimoire Corpus
concepts.definition_short: Grimoire corpus is an Analyst Term for the unstable family of manuscript and printed ritual books attributed to Solomon, Honorius, Raziel, angels, or ancient sages; the portal must track each text individually rather than treating grimoires as interchangeable.
concepts.significance: Grimoire corpus is an Analyst Term for the unstable family of manuscript and printed ritual books attributed to Solomon, Honorius, Raziel, angels, or ancient sages; the portal must track each text individually rather than treating grimoires as interchangeable.

concepts.label: Solomonic Magic
concepts.definition_short: Solomonic magic names traditions that invoke Solomon's authority for spirit command, seals, ritual purity, and secret knowledge; it is both an actor strategy of attribution and a modern scholarly category.
concepts.significance: Solomonic magic names traditions that invoke Solomon's authority for spirit command, seals, ritual purity, and secret knowledge; it is both an actor strategy of attribution and a modern scholarly category.

concepts.label: Scholastic Classification of Magic
concepts.definition_short: Scholastic classification of magic denotes the theological and philosophical sorting of practices into natural, demonic, superstitious, divinatory, or licit forms by medieval intellectuals.
concepts.significance: Scholastic classification of magic denotes the theological and philosophical sorting of practices into natural, demonic, superstitious, divinatory, or licit forms by medieval intellectuals.

concepts.label: Occult Properties
concepts.definition_short: Occult properties are hidden natural powers invoked in scholastic natural philosophy to explain effects not reducible to manifest qualities, creating a crucial boundary zone with natural magic.
concepts.significance: Occult properties are hidden natural powers invoked in scholastic natural philosophy to explain effects not reducible to manifest qualities, creating a crucial boundary zone with natural magic.

concepts.label: Celestial Influence
concepts.definition_short: Celestial influence names medieval theories of astral causation that support astrology, image magic, medicine, and debates over determinism.
concepts.significance: Celestial influence names medieval theories of astral causation that support astrology, image magic, medicine, and debates over determinism.

concepts.label: University Condemnation
concepts.definition_short: University condemnation is an Analyst Term for institutional acts that classified, restricted, or prohibited suspect doctrines and practices, including astrology, image magic, and demonic arts.
concepts.significance: University condemnation is an Analyst Term for institutional acts that classified, restricted, or prohibited suspect doctrines and practices, including astrology, image magic, and demonic arts.

concepts.label: Pastoral Care and Magic
concepts.definition_short: Pastoral care and magic names the confessional, preaching, and catechetical settings in which clergy identified charms, divination, and superstition as problems of Christian discipline.
concepts.significance: Pastoral care and magic names the confessional, preaching, and catechetical settings in which clergy identified charms, divination, and superstition as problems of Christian discipline.

concepts.label: Pseudepigraphy
concepts.definition_short: Pseudepigraphy is an Analyst Term for attribution to authoritative figures such as Solomon, Honorius, Raziel, Aristotle, or Hermes; in grimoire studies it is a central mechanism of textual authority.
concepts.significance: Pseudepigraphy is an Analyst Term for attribution to authoritative figures such as Solomon, Honorius, Raziel, Aristotle, or Hermes; in grimoire studies it is a central mechanism of textual authority.

concepts.label: Ritual Diagrams
concepts.definition_short: Ritual diagrams are visual structures such as circles, notae, seals, tables, and figures that organize ritual knowledge and require attention to manuscript layout and copying.
concepts.significance: Ritual diagrams are visual structures such as circles, notae, seals, tables, and figures that organize ritual knowledge and require attention to manuscript layout and copying.

concepts.label: Magical Alphabets
concepts.definition_short: Magical alphabets are nonordinary scripts and character systems used in ritual texts, amulets, and seals; they are visual technologies of secrecy, authority, and transmission.
concepts.significance: Magical alphabets are nonordinary scripts and character systems used in ritual texts, amulets, and seals; they are visual technologies of secrecy, authority, and transmission.

concepts.label: Planetary Spirits
concepts.definition_short: Planetary spirits are named intelligences, angels, or demons associated with planets in ritual and astral texts, linking astrology to invocation and image practice.
concepts.significance: Planetary spirits are named intelligences, angels, or demons associated with planets in ritual and astral texts, linking astrology to invocation and image practice.

concepts.label: Secret Names
concepts.definition_short: Secret names are divine, angelic, demonic, or voces magicae names whose ritual force is tied to secrecy, antiquity, revelation, or exact textual transmission.
concepts.significance: Secret names are divine, angelic, demonic, or voces magicae names whose ritual force is tied to secrecy, antiquity, revelation, or exact textual transmission.

concepts.label: Experimental Science
concepts.definition_short: Experimental science is an Analyst Term especially associated with older histories such as Thorndike's, where magic and experiment are studied as intertwined medieval attempts to test, command, or explain nature.
concepts.significance: Experimental science is an Analyst Term especially associated with older histories such as Thorndike's, where magic and experiment are studied as intertwined medieval attempts to test, command, or explain nature.

concepts.label: Natural Powers
concepts.definition_short: Natural powers names medieval attempts to explain unusual effects through created nature rather than demonic pact, a key boundary zone between natural philosophy and magic.
concepts.significance: Natural powers names medieval attempts to explain unusual effects through created nature rather than demonic pact, a key boundary zone between natural philosophy and magic.

concepts.label: Prohibited Arts
concepts.definition_short: Prohibited arts is a hybrid category for practices forbidden by theological, legal, university, or pastoral authorities, including forms of divination, image magic, spirit invocation, and suspect astrology.
concepts.significance: Prohibited arts is a hybrid category for practices forbidden by theological, legal, university, or pastoral authorities, including forms of divination, image magic, spirit invocation, and suspect astrology.

concepts.label: Mathematical Arts
concepts.definition_short: Mathematical arts refers to quadrivial and astral disciplines, especially astrology, whose learned status made their relation to divination and magic especially contested.
concepts.significance: Mathematical arts refers to quadrivial and astral disciplines, especially astrology, whose learned status made their relation to divination and magic especially contested.

concepts.label: Licit and Illicit Knowledge
concepts.definition_short: Licit and illicit knowledge is an Analyst Term for medieval debates over what could be known through nature, revelation, experiment, stars, demons, or ritual practice.
concepts.significance: Licit and illicit knowledge is an Analyst Term for medieval debates over what could be known through nature, revelation, experiment, stars, demons, or ritual practice.

concepts.label: Demonology
concepts.definition_short: Demonology is an Analyst Term for systematic learned discussion of demons, their powers, limitations, deception, and relation to divination, magic, superstition, and witchcraft.
concepts.significance: Demonology is an Analyst Term for systematic learned discussion of demons, their powers, limitations, deception, and relation to divination, magic, superstition, and witchcraft.

concepts.label: Witchcraft
concepts.definition_short: Witchcraft is an Analyst Term for accusations, learned demonological categories, and late medieval constructions of harmful magic; it must be distinguished from ritual manuscripts and from broader categories of learned magic.
concepts.significance: Witchcraft is an Analyst Term for accusations, learned demonological categories, and late medieval constructions of harmful magic; it must be distinguished from ritual manuscripts and from broader categories of learned magic.

concepts.label: Exorcism
concepts.definition_short: Exorcism names authorized Christian rites and adjacent ritual practices for expelling or commanding spirits, making it a boundary category between liturgy, pastoral care, and ritual magic.
concepts.significance: Exorcism names authorized Christian rites and adjacent ritual practices for expelling or commanding spirits, making it a boundary category between liturgy, pastoral care, and ritual magic.

concepts.label: Hydromancy
concepts.definition_short: Hydromancy is an Actor Term for divination by water, frequently named in medieval taxonomies of forbidden divination and often treated as suspect because of its association with spirit mediation.
concepts.significance: Hydromancy is an Actor Term for divination by water, frequently named in medieval taxonomies of forbidden divination and often treated as suspect because of its association with spirit mediation.

concepts.label: Pyromancy
concepts.definition_short: Pyromancy is an Actor Term for divination by fire, appearing in medieval lists of mantic arts and classifications of illicit knowledge.
concepts.significance: Pyromancy is an Actor Term for divination by fire, appearing in medieval lists of mantic arts and classifications of illicit knowledge.

concepts.label: Sortilege
concepts.definition_short: Sortilege is an Actor Term for divination by lots, books, or chance procedures, treated variously as superstition, clerical misuse, or illicit inquiry into hidden things.
concepts.significance: Sortilege is an Actor Term for divination by lots, books, or chance procedures, treated variously as superstition, clerical misuse, or illicit inquiry into hidden things.

concepts.label: Notae
concepts.definition_short: Notae are the visual signs or figures central to Ars Notoria traditions of ritual learning, requiring attention to diagrammatic transmission as well as verbal prayer.
concepts.significance: Notae are the visual signs or figures central to Ars Notoria traditions of ritual learning, requiring attention to diagrammatic transmission as well as verbal prayer.

concepts.label: Confession
concepts.definition_short: Confession is a sacramental and pastoral context in which medieval clergy identified charms, divination, superstition, and illicit ritual practices as matters of correction.
concepts.significance: Confession is a sacramental and pastoral context in which medieval clergy identified charms, divination, superstition, and illicit ritual practices as matters of correction.

concepts.label: Secret of Secrets
concepts.definition_short: Secret of Secrets refers to the Secretum Secretorum tradition and its reception as a pseudo-Aristotelian vehicle for princely counsel, occult knowledge, physiognomy, astrology, and medicine.
concepts.significance: Secret of Secrets refers to the Secretum Secretorum tradition and its reception as a pseudo-Aristotelian vehicle for princely counsel, occult knowledge, physiognomy, astrology, and medicine.

concepts.label: Experimenta
concepts.definition_short: Experimenta is an Actor Term for trials, recipes, or procedures transmitted as experiential knowledge; in medieval magic studies it marks the overlap between practical experiment, secrets literature, medicine, and ritual operation.
concepts.significance: Experimenta is an Actor Term for trials, recipes, or procedures transmitted as experiential knowledge; in medieval magic studies it marks the overlap between practical experiment, secrets literature, medicine, and ritual operation.

timeline_events.title: Thabit ibn Qurra and the Sabian milieu
timeline_events.description: c. 875, Harran and Baghdad: Thabit ibn Qurra works within Arabic scientific and philosophical networks later associated in Latin reception with astral image theory. The connection matters for medieval magic scholarship because Latin attributions to Thabit helped frame image magic as learned natural philosophy rather than merely illicit ritual.

timeline_events.title: Latin Picatrix enters western learned culture
timeline_events.description: c. 1250-1300, Iberia and the Latin West: The Arabic Ghayat al-hakim circulates in Latin as the Picatrix, transmitting a large body of astral image theory, ritual timing, planetary correspondences, and philosophical justification. Modern scholars treat this translation history as central to the Arabic-Latin formation of learned magic.

timeline_events.title: Ars Notoria and angelic learning circulate in manuscripts
timeline_events.description: c. 1300-1400, western Europe: Ars Notoria manuscripts transmit prayers, diagrams, and ritual schedules promising divinely assisted learning. The tradition complicates simple oppositions between piety and magic because its procedures often present themselves through Christian prayer while attracting suspicion from theologians and ecclesiastical authorities.

timeline_events.title: Forbidden Rites published
timeline_events.description: 1998, University Park, Pennsylvania: Richard Kieckhefer publishes Forbidden Rites, an edition and study of a fifteenth-century necromancer's manual. The book becomes a landmark for studying medieval ritual magic as manuscript practice, learned clerical culture, and historically specific textual compilation.

timeline_events.title: John of Morigny reworks the Ars Notoria
timeline_events.description: c. 1350, northern France: John of Morigny composes and revises a visionary and ritual work that transforms Ars Notoria materials through Marian devotion, monastic autobiography, and claims of correction. Claire Fanger's work has made this case central for understanding how medieval ritual learning could be simultaneously devotional, visionary, and suspect.

timeline_events.title: Johannes Hartlieb writes on prohibited arts
timeline_events.description: 1456, Bavaria: Johannes Hartlieb composes advice literature for princely readers on forbidden arts, witchcraft, and magic. The work is significant because it joins courtly counsel, medical learning, and moral warning at a moment when late medieval categories of witchcraft and ritual magic were being systematized.

timeline_events.title: Thorndike publishes the first volumes of A History of Magic and Experimental Science
timeline_events.description: 1923, New York: Lynn Thorndike publishes early volumes of A History of Magic and Experimental Science, establishing a vast documentary frame for the entanglement of magic, natural philosophy, astrology, and experimental inquiry. Later scholars have revised Thorndike's evolutionary assumptions while continuing to rely on the scope of his evidence.

timeline_events.title: Benedek Lang publishes Unlocked Books
timeline_events.description: 2008, University Park, Pennsylvania: Benedek Lang publishes Unlocked Books, shifting attention toward Central European manuscript libraries, ownership, and codicological evidence. The study broadens medieval magic scholarship beyond famous Latin treatises toward the practical survival of learned magic in library collections.

timeline_events.title: Secretum Secretorum enters Latin learned culture
timeline_events.description: c. 1140-1160, Iberia and the Latin West: The pseudo-Aristotelian Secretum Secretorum circulates in Latin as a flexible vehicle for princely counsel, physiognomy, medicine, astrology, and hidden knowledge. Its importance for medieval magic lies not in being a grimoire, but in showing how political advice, natural philosophy, and occultized secrets could travel under Aristotelian authority.

timeline_events.title: Albertus Magnus treats minerals and occult natural powers
timeline_events.description: c. 1250-1270, Cologne and the Dominican schools: Albertus Magnus discusses stones, minerals, and hidden natural powers in works such as De mineralibus. The episode matters because scholastic natural philosophy offered categories for unusual effects that could be treated as natural rather than demonic, shaping later debates over natural magic and occult properties.

timeline_events.title: Hartlieb writes the Book of All Forbidden Arts
timeline_events.description: 1456, Bavaria: Johannes Hartlieb writes the Buch aller verbotenen Kunst for a princely milieu, classifying and warning against prohibited arts, witchcraft, divination, and magical practices. The text matters because it joins vernacular advice, moral instruction, and late medieval concern with illicit knowledge before the full consolidation of early modern witchcraft theory.
